annotation_description: Choosing to play first with a hand full of reactive spells (Spell Pierce, two Spell Snares) and only one proactive card (Sleight of Hand). Playing first means drawing one fewer card and having reactive counterspells that are better on the draw when you have more cards and your opponent acts first. This hand is heavily skewed toward interaction rather than proactive threats.

Riverpyre Verge enters tapped on turn 1 since GLM47 controls no Island or Mountain, so it can only produce colorless (just {R}) this turn and cannot produce {U} yet. Meanwhile, Spirebluff Canal enters untapped when you control two or fewer other lands (this would be the first land, so 0 others), producing {U} or {R} immediately. Playing Spirebluff Canal first would allow casting Sleight of Hand on turn 1 to dig for better cards, or holding up Spell Pierce / Spell Snare. With Riverpyre Verge, GLM47 can only tap for {R} (no Island/Mountain yet to enable the {U} mode), so none of the 1-mana spells in hand (all requiring {U}) can be cast this turn.

Playing Breeding Pool turn 1 instead of Gloomlake Verge wastes 2 life (if entering untapped) or tempo (if entering tapped). Gloomlake Verge enters untapped for free and produces U for Spell Snare. On turn 2, playing a typed dual (Watery Grave or Breeding Pool) would then enable Gloomlake Verge's B production as well.

Chose Steam Vents over Abandon Attachments when the hand already contained Spirebluff Canal as a guaranteed land drop for turn 3. The hand was loaded with cheap reactive spells (Spell Pierce, 2x Spell Snare, Burst Lightning) but lacked any card advantage or threats. Abandon Attachments would provide a way to convert redundant reactive cards into fresh draws, which is more valuable than a 4th land in a hand full of 1-mana spells.

Underground Mortuary enters tapped, meaning KimiK2 will have only 1 mana available this turn (Breeding Pool). Playing Watery Grave (paying 2 life to have it enter untapped) would give 2 mana available, enabling casting Spell Snare or Sleight of Hand this turn while still having U/B mana. Alternatively, Gloomlake Verge enters untapped and can tap for U (since Breeding Pool is an Island), giving 2 mana. Either untapped land would be strictly better here since having 2 mana up on turn 2 is important for holding up Spell Snare against the opponent's turn-2 play. Underground Mortuary's surveil 1 is a small upside but not worth losing a full turn of mana development.

Spirebluff Canal enters untapped for free when you control 2 or fewer other lands (currently at 2 lands total, so playing it as the 3rd land means 2 other lands). Playing Steam Vents instead either costs 2 life to enter untapped or enters tapped. On a later turn when they have 3+ other lands, Spirebluff Canal would enter tapped, so it's strictly better to play it now.

Casting Burst Lightning at the opponent's face for 2 damage when they're at 20 life is extremely low-value. This burn spell would be much better saved to remove a creature later. The opponent has no creatures currently but could deploy threats that Burst Lightning could answer (e.g., small creatures, or combined with other damage). Throwing away a removal spell for 2 damage at 20 life accomplishes almost nothing.

Awaken the Honored Dead costs {B}{G}{U} (3 mana, one of each color), which is exactly what the three lands produce (Breeding Pool for G/U, Underground Mortuary for B/G, Gloomlake Verge for U/B). It would destroy a target nonland permanent on chapter I, removing one of the opponent's lands/permanents while the opponent only has 3 lands and no creatures. However, Formidable Speaker also costs 3 mana ({2}{G}) and puts a 2/4 body on board. The key consideration is that Awaken the Honored Dead could destroy Steam Vents (reducing opponent to 2 mana sources and potentially cutting them off colors), which is a strong tempo play. Formidable Speaker is a solid on-curve creature but the player chose not to discard anything, missing the tutor ability. Without the tutor trigger, the Speaker is just a vanilla 2/4 on turn 3. The Saga would provide immediate interaction (destroying a permanent) plus future value (mill + card return). Given the opponent has open mana for potential countermagic and the player's hand is heavy with expensive cards, both plays have merit, but the Saga destroying Steam Vents could be a significant tempo swing.

Ardyn, the Usurper costs 8 mana (5BBB) and is extremely difficult to cast in this deck. The player is on turn 3 with only 3 lands and needs a card that can impact the board soon. Overlord of the Balemurk can be cast for its impending cost of just 1B as early as next turn, providing mill and recursion value while building toward a 5/5 body. Bringer of the Last Gift is also expensive but has a devastating ETB. Harvester of Misery at 3BB is much more castable and provides immediate board impact with its -2/-2 effect. Searching for Ardyn is searching for a card that likely won't be castable for many turns, if ever, in a game where tempo matters.

GLM47 cast Glacial Dragonhunt (a spell) before playing a land for the turn. They have both Spirebluff Canal and Multiversal Passage in hand and haven't played a land yet this turn. Playing a land first is almost always correct sequencing — it preserves options and leaves more mana available after casting spells. Specifically, playing Spirebluff Canal first (which enters untapped since they control exactly 3 lands after playing it... wait, they already have 3 lands, so it would enter tapped). Multiversal Passage could enter untapped if they pay 2 life. Either way, playing the land first costs nothing and could matter if they draw into or need to respond with Spell Pierce or Spell Snare later. The Glacial Dragonhunt costs UR which uses all their available mana anyway, so the land play would need to come after. However, in post-combat main, playing the land first still preserves information and is strictly better sequencing — they could play the land, then cast the spell, ending with more mana available for opponent's turn responses.

annotation_description: Spirebluff Canal enters tapped because they control 3+ other lands, leaving only 1 untapped land (Island). Playing Riverpyre Verge instead would enter untapped (since they control an Island and Mountain), giving 2 untapped lands and more flexibility to hold up multiple counterspells (Spell Pierce + Spell Snare) on the opponent's turn.

Casting Bitter Triumph with no creatures on the opponent's board is a waste of a removal spell. The opponent has only lands in play - no creatures or planeswalkers to target. Additionally, Bitter Triumph requires discarding a card or paying 3 life as an additional cost, so this wastes both the spell and an additional resource for nothing. The player should have played Watery Grave as their land drop and then cast Awaken the Honored Dead (which at least provides value through its saga chapters) or simply developed their board.

KimiK2 cast Awaken the Honored Dead (BGU) before playing Watery Grave from hand. By playing the land first, they would have had access to an additional mana source this turn. While they have exactly 3 lands untapped (Breeding Pool, Underground Mortuary, Gloomlake Verge) to cast the BGU saga, playing Watery Grave first would leave an extra land available after casting the saga — or more importantly, would allow them to hold up Spell Snare (U) after casting the saga if they played the land first and used different mana sequencing. With 4 lands they could cast Awaken the Honored Dead and still have 1 mana open for Spell Snare. By casting the spell first, they use all 3 available lands and cannot play Watery Grave with any mana remaining for interaction.

GLM47 cast Opt during their own main phase before playing a land. They have two lands in hand (Multiversal Passage and Riverpyre Verge) but only need to play one. By casting Opt first, they spend mana before seeing if the land drop matters, and more importantly, Opt is an instant that could be cast at end of opponent's turn to keep mana open for Spell Snare during the opponent's turn. Playing a land first costs nothing and preserves the option to hold up Opt + Spell Snare mana. However, since they have two Spell Snares and will have 4 lands after playing one, they can still hold up Spell Snare after casting Opt. The main issue is that Opt should generally be cast at end of opponent's turn to maximize information and flexibility, not during your own main phase.

GLM47 Libby cast Sleight of Hand before playing a land. They have both Multiversal Passage and Riverpyre Verge in hand and need to play one this turn to not miss a land drop. By casting Sleight of Hand first, they spend mana before seeing if the land drop matters for sequencing, and more importantly, if they draw a land off Sleight of Hand, they might want to play that instead. However, since they have two lands already in hand, this is less impactful — they're guaranteed to make a land drop regardless. The main issue is that playing the land first (Multiversal Passage) would leave all four lands untapped after playing it, preserving the same mana while guaranteeing the land drop. If Sleight of Hand reveals something that changes which land they want to play, casting it first could be slightly better. But conventionally, you should play the land first to avoid accidentally missing the drop if something unexpected happens, and Multiversal Passage entering untapped (paying 2 life) would still leave the same mana available.

KimiK2 should play Wastewood Verge as their land drop before casting Superior Spider-Man. Playing the land first costs nothing and leaves more mana available after casting the Spider-Man (5 lands instead of 4, with one untapped). Additionally, casting Superior Spider-Man before combat means the opponent knows the board state before blocks matter, and more importantly, the player should consider whether to hold up Spell Snare (1 mana) as protection. However, the bigger issue is sequencing: land drop should always come before spending mana on spells when there's no reason to delay it.

Superior Spider-Man's Mind Swap ability lets it enter as a copy of a creature card in a graveyard as a 4/4 with additional types. Declining this is passing up significant value. Copying Sunderflock (a 5/5 flyer that bounces all non-Elementals when cast - though the ETB won't trigger since it checks 'if you cast it') would give a 4/4 flyer, which is strictly better than a vanilla 4/4. Copying Harvester of Misery would give a 4/4 with menace plus trigger its ETB giving all other creatures -2/-2, which could be devastating against the opponent's board. The player's reasoning shows confusion about the cards - calling Sunderflock a 'smaller mana dork' and Harvester a '3/3 with menace' when it's actually a 5/4 with menace and a powerful ETB. This is declining a pure-upside ability that would have added flying or menace+board wipe to the 4/4 body, plus exiling the copied card from the graveyard (relevant since opponent could potentially use those cards).

Cast Formidable Speaker precombat when Superior Spider-Man could attack unblocked first. While the opponent has no creatures, standard practice is to attack before committing more resources to the board precombat, preserving information and mana flexibility. The opponent has 2 untapped lands and plays counterspells.

Searched for Bringer of the Last Gift (costs 8 mana) when they only have 6 lands and need immediate board development. Overlord of the Balemurk could be cast THIS TURN for its impending cost of {1}{B}, immediately starting to mill cards and generate value while eventually becoming a 5/5 threat. Against a spell-heavy opponent with no creatures, getting Overlord down immediately provides much more pressure than a Bringer that's 2+ turns away from being castable.

Chose Glacial Dragonhunt (Harmonize) over Winternight Stories (Harmonize) from graveyard. Glacial Dragonhunt costs all 6 mana for draw 1 + conditional 3 damage (which doesn't kill the 2/4 Formidable Speaker anyway). Winternight Stories costs only 5 mana for draw 3 (discard 2 or 1 creature), providing much better card advantage and leaving 1 mana open for Spell Snare in hand.

annotation_description: Glacial Dragonhunt only deals 3 damage to a target creature when you discard a NONLAND card. By discarding Spirebluff Canal (a land), the damage ability never triggers, completely wasting the removal mode of the spell. The opponent has creatures on board (Formidable Speaker, Superior Spider-Man) that could have been targeted.

At 4 life with many lands already in play, Spirebluff Canal will always enter tapped (more than 2 other lands). Steam Vents at least has the option of entering untapped in the future if life total allows. Playing the land with no future upside first is correct sequencing.

The player's reasoning states Bitter Triumph can kill the opponent at 4 life, but Bitter Triumph only destroys creatures or planeswalkers - it cannot target players. Meanwhile, they have lethal on board: Superior Spider-Man (4/4) + Formidable Speaker (2/4) = 6 damage against an opponent at 4 life with everything tapped. Casting Bitter Triumph wastes a card and resources (discard or 3 life) unnecessarily.

Opponent is at 4 life with all permanents tapped. The only blocker (Eddymurk Crab) is tapped. Destroying the Crab with Bitter Triumph and attacking with Superior Spider-Man (4) + Formidable Speaker (2) = 6 damage is lethal. Instead, KimiK2 targeted their own Superior Spider-Man with Bitter Triumph, destroying their best attacker and wasting removal.
